rankings.blurb: Four Cornerstones including the best QB-RB-WR-TE combo in the league — Drake Maye, Jahmyr Gibbs, Puka Nacua, and Trey McBride is an absurd roster foundation. Yes, they overpaid for Gibbs according to the trade calculator, but when you acquire a 9,900 KTC asset you don't cry about losing a pick haul — you cash the check. The pick cupboard is thin with only one first, but when your player core looks like this, you don't need a rebuild plan. Everyone else is playing for second place.

Eleven Cornerstones and Foundational assets — ELEVEN — and this roster is somehow only ranked second. Ja'Marr Chase, JSN, Drake London, Jayden Daniels, De'Von Achane, Omarion Hampton: this is what a dynasty powerhouse looks like. The TE room is the one thing keeping this team from being an untouchable tyrant, but Colston Loveland is a rising tide. They've been getting fleeced in trades lately — losing value to Hernandez and paying too much for Bucky Irving — so Sven needs to put the pen down and let the roster cook.

Seven first-round picks and the most total dynasty value in the league — this is what a reload looks like when it's done right. Caleb Williams as a Cornerstone QB, Jeremiyah Love as a 7,500 KTC rocket, Jaxson Dart as a stashed upside bomb, and Harold Fannin at TE — the future is so bright you need sunglasses. The unloading of Trey McBride and Breece Hall to stack picks was chess while everyone else was playing checkers. The only knock is there's no win-now push, but with this asset base, the coronation is coming.

Josh Allen is a 9,998 KTC cheat code and Ashton Jeanty is already threatening to be the next elite RB cornerstone — that's a core that makes other owners physically ill. The WR room of Garrett Wilson, Zay Flowers, and Jaylen Waddle is a solid foundational trio even if none of them are elite. The TE spot is a tire fire with Sam LaPorta leading the charge like a reluctant hall monitor. That trade giving up Shough and a first for Mayfield and Garrett Wilson is puzzling — getting Wilson back is nice, but Shough was the future QB2.

Joe Burrow and Jalen Hurts at QB is an embarrassment of riches, and Amon-Ra St. Brown plus Nico Collins gives this team real WR production. But whoever made that trade giving away two 2029 firsts AND Jameson Williams to get Malik Willis and Michael Wilson back needs to be investigated by the league — that's a catastrophic heist that nchernandez practically robbed at gunpoint. Zero first-round picks remaining is a death sentence if the injury bug bites, and the RB room of aging Jonathan Taylor and recently traded Breece Hall is a walking red flag. This team is living in the present and pretending there's no future.

Bijan Robinson and Brock Bowers in the same rebuild is downright unfair — most teams would kill for one of those assets, and nchernandez has both anchoring a rebuild. Six first-round picks in the war chest and a trail of robbery victims behind him (GiantHawkTua called, they'd like their picks back), this team is operating like a dynasty loan shark. Jordan Love at QB is a legitimate question mark, and the WR room behind Marvin Harrison is a wasteland of vibes and prayers. But the asset base is so strong that this team is going to be terrifying in 24 months.

Seven first-round picks is a war chest, but trading away Ja'Marr Chase — one of the top dynasty assets in existence — means this team willingly burned its own house down hoping the new one gets built faster. Malik Nabers as a lone Cornerstone is a fine foundation, but Fernando Mendoza as your QB1 and Bhayshul Tuten leading the backfield is a lineup that would make a participation trophy wince. The pick haul is real, but the player core underneath it is so thin it's basically just vibes and future promises. Enjoy your Skyline Chili in the dark, Akracoon.

Justin Jefferson and CeeDee Lamb at WR is a beautiful dream sitting in a crumbling dynasty house. Brock Purdy is a Foundational QB but let's not pretend he's franchise-altering, and the RB room of aging McCaffrey, Chase Brown, and Saquon Barkley is a ticking time bomb of declining legs and injury risk. Zero picks beyond one first means this team has no draft-day escape hatch when the vets start falling apart — and they will. The window is either right now or never, and the trade history suggests GreyWaedekin is rearranging deck chairs on the Titanic.

Lamar Jackson AND Patrick Mahomes at QB sounds incredible until you realize the rest of this roster is an absolute graveyard — Derrick Henry leading the RB room, Travis Kelce at TE, and Daniel Jones as QB3 is a museum exhibit called 'What Winning Looked Like in 2022.' Zero future picks. Zero. That's not a rebuild plan, that's a last will and testament. A.J. Brown and Tee Higgins are solid foundational WRs but both are aging in a room that has no young reload behind them. This team is sprinting toward a cliff and calling it a contender window.

Five firsts and a pile of roster question marks — this is a rebuild that smells like potential but tastes like uncertainty. Tyler Shough as your QB1, TreVeyon Henderson leading your backfield, and George Kittle as a short-term TE rental is not a dynasty roster, it's a fantasy garage sale. George Pickens is a legitimate Foundational WR and Travis Hunter is a tantalizing stash, but the starting lineup right now would get cooked by half the league. Seth was smart enough to fleece ekleiner for the Gibbs trade and pivot out of the veteran window — now comes the hard part of actually building something worth watching.
